title: Pain reduction after cholecystectomy with obliquus externus nerve blockade
summary:
Cholecystectomy, the removal of the gallbladder, is one of the most common surgical procedures in the field of abdominal surgery in Germany. 
Today, the gallbladder is usually removed using the so-called laparoscopic method. Even though this method is less painful than open surgery, pain can still occur after the procedure.

Medication such as ibuprofen (NSAIDs), paracetamol or, in more severe cases, opioids (strong painkillers) are often used to reduce postoperative pain. As opioids have side effects, attempts are being made to minimise their use. Other methods are therefore increasingly being used, e.g. nerve blocks, in which certain nerves are specifically anaesthetised.

The study described here investigates a special type of nerve block, the right-sided external oblique nerve block. An anaesthetic is administered using ultrasound to test whether this can reduce pain after the operation, particularly in the first three hours. The aim is for patients to recover more quickly, be able to move again sooner and require less strong painkillers (opioids).

interventions.name: Control group: standard treatment in the meaning of a selective minimally invasive cholecystectomy

Intervention group: Additional application of an external oblique nerve block on the right side with 20 ml ropivacaine 0.375% (150mg in total) using a 22G 80mm needle from BBraun under sonographic guidance.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Planned minimally invasive cholecystectomy
ASA status 1 or 2
BMI < 30 kg/m2
Exclusion criteria:
No planned operation
Other surgical technique
Extension of the operation
BMI >=30 kg/m2
ASA status >= 3
Inability to understand or answer the questions
Allergy to any of the medications used
